title: Mold factory
text:
Mold factory. I have given this product about a month of consistent use to rate it fairly. While I can say it is aesthetically pleasing and produces a nice amount of humidity, the mold growth is without precedent in my experience.

I am no stranger to humidifiers - being an older person with lifelong sinus and allergy problems. I had a faithful Holmes tabletop model that was probably bigger than this by a half. It lasted me ten years using distilled water. Never in 10 winters did I get any mold. I emptied and wiped it dry every other day. And use bleach once a week.

I initially loved this. Nice amount of moisture, no noise and with distilled water of course no white powder. After two weeks of use, emptying every other day just like I did with the Holmes I was greeted with a stench of mold. I had to look closely but saw the bottom of the blue water tank was covered with moldy slightly raaised bumps. I could just manage to stick a finger in the hole and wipe at them, so I knew they were organic. A soak with bleach and all was well. I had been carrying on with an every other day bleach until this morning I noticed a weird pattern, dark kind of abstract on the inside "hump" of the water tank. It actually looked like something metallic maybe had scratched. I gave it the usual bleach treatment while I was at work and found the "pattern" still there. I was going to write it off as some sort of scratches but decided to dig out a pipe cleaner to see if I could reach. Yep, pipe cleaner cleaned off the "scratches" more mold.

I can't believe how many different varieties(s) of mold this thing can grow. It is like some petri dish! It is not in the sun. It is only filled with cold distilled water. Why is this happening?

My trusty old Holmes which is not sold anymore (and I couldn't find ANYthing like it) had a huge water fill thing with a gasket and you could get your whole hand in there (if you weren't like a really big boned person) to clean if necessary. This thing forget it. And frankly the design of all of them are like this now.

I am trying just to get through the season with this. Will look into some bottle brushes that can maybe be bent to reach critical areas of mold habitation. A shame because it really runs nice.
